body:
Devon Ricci: Welcome to your Voxly kickoff, everyone. Kayla, Tom — really excited to have Acme onboard. This meeting we'll walk through the ninety-day plan, confirm the integration approach, and align on success metrics. Sound good?

Kayla Nguyen: Perfect. Yeah, we're excited too. The pilot data looked great.

Tom Brenner: Agreed. And the sandbox environment worked out of the box, which was refreshing.

Devon Ricci: Love hearing that. So, phase one, weeks one through three — Marcus and Tom will pair on the Zendesk connector and the intent taxonomy. Phase two, weeks four through six, we'll do a soft launch on ten percent of inbound. Phase three, weeks seven through twelve, ramp to full volume with weekly tuning sessions.

Marcus Fields: Tom, on the Zendesk side you mentioned you're using triggers to auto-assign tickets — we'll want to make sure our bot-created tickets fire the right triggers. Should be straightforward.

Tom Brenner: Yeah, that's fine. I already looked at the API docs you sent. It's a clean integration. I don't foresee issues.

Kayla Nguyen: What about the intent taxonomy? We've got about twelve top-level categories today.

Devon Ricci: We'll do a workshop in week two — I'll bring one of our conversation designers. We usually consolidate down to six or eight top-level intents for v1, because higher granularity than that tends to hurt classification accuracy. It's not a hard rule though.

Kayla Nguyen: Makes sense. We're flexible on that.

Marcus Fields: One more thing on integration — you mentioned you have a custom knowledge base at kb.acmecorp.io. Is that on Notion or something custom?

Tom Brenner: It's Notion. We can give you a service account with read access to the public spaces.

Marcus Fields: Perfect. Our Notion connector handles that natively. I'll send you the OAuth setup docs after this call.

Devon Ricci: Success metrics — Kayla, what do you want to hit by the end of ninety days?

Kayla Nguyen: Honestly, the two big ones are containment rate above forty percent and CSAT parity with human agents. If we hit both of those I'm a happy person.

Devon Ricci: Those are reasonable targets. Our median customer at your call volume hits about forty-seven percent containment by day ninety, and CSAT is usually within two points of human baseline by then.

Kayla Nguyen: Great, that's encouraging.

Tom Brenner: What kind of engineering time do we need to budget on our side over the ninety days?

Marcus Fields: Roughly? Twenty hours in weeks one through three, ten hours a week during soft launch, and then it drops to maybe two hours a week steady state.

Tom Brenner: That's manageable.

Devon Ricci: We'll have a weekly forty-five minute sync every Tuesday, and I'll be your day-to-day contact for anything that comes up. Slack channel is already provisioned — I'll drop the invite after the call.

Kayla Nguyen: Perfect. Who else should be in the Slack channel from your side?

Devon Ricci: Me, Marcus, and our on-call SRE rotation. If we hit a production incident during business hours you'll get a response within fifteen minutes.

Tom Brenner: What's the escalation path for after-hours?

Devon Ricci: For sev-one incidents, PagerDuty. I'll set up your team as authorized escalation contacts in our on-call system.

Tom Brenner: Great.

Marcus Fields: One more thing on the technical side — sandbox and production are separate environments, so any tuning we do in staging you'll want to promote explicitly. We have a one-click promote flow but you should know it's not auto-sync.

Tom Brenner: Understood. That's how we operate anyway.

Kayla Nguyen: What about reporting? What's built-in for me to look at week-over-week?

Devon Ricci: The v1 dashboard has containment rate, CSAT proxy scores, top intents, and handle time trends. If you want deeper analytics — like intent-level containment breakdown or per-agent handoff analysis — that's the analytics addon.

Kayla Nguyen: The default sounds sufficient for phase one. We can revisit the addon later.

Kayla Nguyen: Awesome. This all feels well-organized.

Devon Ricci: One last thing — we like to celebrate wins. When we hit that forty percent containment milestone I'm sending your team lunch. Just so you know.

Kayla Nguyen: Ha, deal.

Tom Brenner: I'm holding you to that.

Devon Ricci: You should. Alright, action items — Marcus sends Notion docs, Tom provisions the Zendesk sandbox account by Friday, Kayla confirms the intent workshop attendees, and I send the ninety-day plan doc to everyone by end of day tomorrow. Anything else?

Kayla Nguyen: Nope, we're good.

Tom Brenner: All clear.

Tom Brenner: Actually, before we wrap — question about voice quality. Any way to preview what the bot sounds like?

Marcus Fields: Yes. I'll share three voice options after the call. You can pick one during the workshop.

Kayla Nguyen: What about pronouncing our product names? We have a product called Acmex-Pro that our IVR mangles.

Marcus Fields: We can add phonetic overrides. Just send us your product name list.

Kayla Nguyen: Perfect. That's a specific pain point that made our current IVR feel really cheap.

Devon Ricci: Perfect. Talk Tuesday.

Kayla Nguyen: Thanks all.

Tom Brenner: Later.
